source.title: Knowledge distillation through geometry-aware representational alignment
source.authors: Prajjwal Bhattarai; Mohammad Amjad; Dmytro Zhylko; Tuka Alhanai

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study compares similarity measures and reports that some can indicate good alignment while the feature geometry remains poorly preserved, refining the claim about metric dependence.
record.gate_note: The synthetic experiments directly optimize alignment objectives and measure CKA and approximate orthogonality, so those results are included. BERT and OPT results report task performance after distillation, not measured representational convergence, and are not rows. The paper also describes theoretical results, but they are not empirical outcome rows.
record.test_reason: This is a knowledge-distillation paper. It optimizes student representations directly toward a teacher using CKA, linear projection, Gram-matrix and Procrustes losses, so alignment is induced on purpose. It then reports which loss best preserves geometry and the distilled models' task scores. It never measures convergence arising between independently trained models. Its synthetic result that low CKA distance can coexist with poor geometry preservation is a measure-validity point, not a test of V6, which concerns measured convergence of independently trained models. That result is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue, theoretically and in a synthetic experiment, that CKA and learned linear projection losses do not reliably preserve teacher feature geometry, while Procrustes (and Gram-matrix distance) do. Procrustes was the more stable of the two; Gram-matrix distance fluctuated. As distillation losses, these gave small but statistically significant gains on BERT GLUE tasks and OPT instruction-following, up to about 2 points.
record.recipe_differences: The study optimizes teacher–student distillation objectives and compares alignment metrics in synthetic representations; it does not reproduce a study of independently trained model convergence across scale.
record.method_sensitivity: Synthetic geometry results differ by objective; Procrustes is described as more structurally stable than Gram distance, and random student initialization changes the room for further orthogonality gains.

fits_no_version.finding: In a synthetic setup, students optimized to near-zero CKA distance from a teacher lost many approximately orthogonal vectors. Procrustes and Gram-matrix objectives preserved more. A theorem shows CKA distance ≤ ε while the Gram-matrix distance can be O(n). (Section 4, Theorem 1; Section 5.1, Figure 2.)
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low CKA distance (high linear CKA) can coexist with substantially different feature geometry, so CKA can overstate representational alignment relative to Procrustes or Gram-matrix distance.

record.problems: The direct geometry comparison is synthetic and relies on figure-only values; numerical geometry results and uncertainty are not stated in the text. The empirical BERT and OPT experiments report task scores rather than representational convergence.
record.rows_left_out: No direct alignment rows were omitted. Task-performance results in Tables 1–3 were left out because they measure downstream performance, not the representational convergence at issue.

untested.parts: All: no comparison of independently trained models across scale or capability.
All: no comparison of networks trained from different seeds.
All: no test of mapping or stitching between independently trained models; alignment is trained in.
All: no cross-model feature or circuit recurrence.
Metric dependence of measured convergence between independently trained models; neighbour settings; input or out-of-distribution dependence.
All: no measure of incomplete or plateauing convergence, and no causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'tested' guess is rejected: all synthetic rows involve optimizing the student toward the teacher, so alignment is induced rather than measured as it arises. The paper cites Moschella et al. on preserved relative angles as motivation only. One reading point: Figure 2b reports 'CKA close to 0'. Given the definitions, this most plausibly means CKA distance, i.e. high CKA.

versions.untested_parts: Scale and capability trends across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
Cross-modal alignment of paired images and captions as vision and language models improve.
Feature or subspace convergence across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
Whether representations are interchangeable through mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired methods.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
The study varies the similarity objective in synthetic experiments, but does not test neighbour-count settings, alternative input distributions, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete across independently trained models, and whether shared data or objectives explain it.
